findings.source_quote: τῶν γὰρ μελλόντων λόγων ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ πρὸς διάκρισιν τῶν ἀγνοούντων λέγεσθαι σὺ πρὸ τῆς ζητήσεως ἐφοδιασθεὶς ὑπ’ ἐμοῦ ἄπτωτος ἀκροατὴς γενέσθαι δυνήσει.
findings.english_quote: for before the debate, having been equipped by me in advance with the arguments that he is going to present for the testing of those who do not know, you will be able to become a hearer who does not stumble.
findings.issue: The fronted genitive τῶν ... λόγων naturally supplies the object of hearing with ἀκροατής: Clement can become an unstumbling hearer of Simon’s forthcoming arguments. The draft instead attaches it to being equipped and explicitly says that Clement has been equipped with those arguments. That changes the relation expressed and leaves the attachment decision undisclosed.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose: “for, having been equipped by me before the debate, you will be able to hear without stumbling the arguments he is going to present for the testing of those who do not know.” If retaining the attachment to ἐφοδιασθείς, establish its grammatical basis and disclose the alternative attachment to ἀκροατής. The replacement requires fresh review.

findings.source_quote: τὰ κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ γραφέντα φιληκόως ἔχειν
findings.english_quote: fondly to accept the things written against God
findings.issue: φιληκόως expresses being fond of hearing or eager to listen. “Fondly to accept” replaces that auditory attitude with acceptance, and the lexical note likewise fails to preserve the hearing component. This matters because the contrasting group refuses even to hear the allegations.
findings.suggested_revision: Propose “eagerly to listen to the things written against God,” and revise the note to explain the fondness-for-hearing sense and its contrast with ἀκούειν. Review the revised clause afresh.

findings.source_quote: τοῖς δὲ εὐγνωμονοῦσιν τῶν κατὰ τοῦ θεοῦ ῥηθεισῶν περικοπῶν μετὰ πεῖραν πίστεως ἰδίᾳ παρέχειν τὴν ἐπίλυσιν
findings.english_quote: but privately to furnish the solution, after a test of faith, to those who judge sensibly concerning the passages spoken against God.
findings.issue: The note records the chosen attachment of τῶν ... περικοπῶν to εὐγνωμονοῦσιν but omits the materially different attachment to τὴν ἐπίλυσιν: providing fair-minded or well-disposed people with the solution of the passages. That alternative specifies the solution’s content rather than the recipients’ object of judgment. The existing disclosure of the earlier coordination ellipsis does not address this uncertainty.
findings.suggested_revision: Either propose “but privately, after a test of faith, to provide those who are fair-minded with the explanation of the passages spoken against God,” or retain the current contextual rendering while adding the genitive-with-ἐπίλυσιν alternative and explaining the basis for preferring the chosen attachment. This is an interpretive attachment question, not evidence of source corruption. Any replacement requires fresh review.

findings.english_quote: you will find gratification beyond compare.
findings.issue: The spelling difficulty and conjecture are disclosed, but the main rendering still lacks adequate lexical support. Reading χαρίσῃ as future middle does not itself establish an experiencer sense, “find gratification.” χαρίζομαι ordinarily expresses showing or granting favor, or gratifying someone; an unspecified recipient does not automatically make the subject the recipient. The proposed χαρήσῃ would support rejoicing, but the draft expressly says that reading is not adopted.
findings.suggested_revision: Retain the verified printed χαρίσῃ and substantiate an attested, contextually applicable absolute or reflexive sense meaning “find gratification.” Without that evidence, propose wording based on the printed verb’s benefactive sense, such as “you will show favor beyond compare,” leaving the recipient unspecified and disclosing the contextual difficulty. Keep χαρήσῃ explicitly identified as a conjecture rather than using its meaning to justify χαρίσῃ. Re-review any replacement. The verified spelling alone does not warrant an OCR allegation or a source-verification block.
